{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "Create a static, responsive marketing website for a friendly moving company called “MoveNest Updates” that presents the company like a ProductHunt-style launch/changelog page. This should be a polished front-end only website with mock/sample content, no backend, no login, no database, no live APIs, and no external services required.

PROJECT GOAL
Build a modern landing page that shows customers what has recently improved about the moving service: new packing options, better booking flow, safer furniture handling, updated pricing bundles, eco-friendly boxes, faster local moves, and seasonal moving tips. The site should feel like a friendly changelog + launch page, inspired by ProductHunt: bold hero, upvote-style visual elements, release cards, tags, comments/testimonials, maker notes, and clear CTAs.

STYLE DIRECTION
- Friendly, warm, optimistic, trustworthy
- ProductHunt-inspired layout but NOT a clone
- Clean white background with soft orange accents, warm navy text, light peach sections, and subtle card shadows
- Rounded UI, simple icons, pill badges, stacked cards, clear hierarchy
- Should look like a startup launch page for a moving company update feed
- Avoid corporate coldness; make it approachable and helpful

TECH / DELIVERABLE
- Use React for a static front-end page
- No backend implementation
- No authentication, accounts, dashboards, payments, CRUD, or real booking system
- All content can be hardcoded mock/static sample content
- Fully responsive for desktop, tablet, and mobile
- Use simple UI components and clean CSS
- It should render as a static site without needing third-party APIs

PAGE STRUCTURE

1. TOP NAVIGATION
- Logo text: MoveNest
- Small badge: “Changelog”
- Nav links: Updates, Services, Why It Matters, Reviews, FAQ
- CTA button: “Plan My Move”
- Sticky or semi-sticky top bar is okay
- Mobile menu can be simple stacked navigation; no complex logic needed

2. HERO SECTION
Headline:
“Moving just got a whole lot easier.”
Subheadline:
“See what’s new at MoveNest — smarter packing, faster estimates, friendlier crews, and stress-free moving updates released every month.”

Hero elements:
- ProductHunt-like launch card showing:
  - “MoveNest Spring Moving Update”
  - Tagline: “Fewer surprises. Softer landings.”
  - Mock upvote count: 486
  - Category pills: Local Moves, Packing, Storage, Eco Boxes
  - CTA buttons: “View Latest Updates” and “Get a Free Estimate”
- Add a small “Today’s update” pill
- Friendly illustration placeholder or abstract moving truck/card layout using CSS shapes only if no image assets are available

3. FEATURED CHANGELOG / RELEASE FEED
Create a section title:
“Latest improvements from the MoveNest team”
Include 5–6 changelog cards with dates, release tags, short descriptions, and small visual icons.

Example changelog items:
- “Room-by-room packing labels” — Color-coded labels now come with every packing kit
- “2-hour arrival windows” — Narrower arrival estimates for local moves
- “Furniture blanket guarantee” — Extra padding for dining tables, dressers, and fragile wood pieces
- “Eco box return program” — Reusable boxes can be picked up after your move
- “Apartment move checklist” — New printable checklist for elevator reservations and loading zones
- “Weekend saver bundles” — Simple bundled pricing examples for Saturday and Sunday moves

Each card should include:
- Date
- Badge like “New”, “Improved”, “Popular”, or “Guide”
- Short 2–3 sentence copy
- Tiny fake metric such as “92 families used this last month” or “4.9 helpful rating”

4. PRODUCTHUNT-STYLE LAUNCH PANEL
Create a central panel that feels like a launch discussion card:
- Title: “Why we shipped this update”
- Maker note from “Lena, Move Coordinator” explaining the company listened to customers who wanted clearer timelines, fewer packing questions, and better protection for furniture
- Include 3 mock comment cards from customers:
  - “The room labels saved us hours.”
  - “The narrower arrival window was a huge relief.”
  - “Eco boxes made the move feel less wasteful.”
- Include a fake “Helpful” button or count as static UI only

5. SERVICES SNAPSHOT
Section title:
“Moving services improved in this release”
Display 4 service cards:
- Local Home Moves
- Apartment & Condo Moves
- Packing Help
- Short-Term Storage

Each service card should include:
- Icon or emoji-style visual
- Short description
- What changed recently
- A small “Learn more” visual link that does not need to navigate anywhere real

6. BEFORE / AFTER COMPARISON
Create a comparison section:
Title: “Before the update vs. now”
Two columns:
Before:
- Unclear packing supply counts
- Wide arrival windows
- Fragile items handled case by case
- Customers printed their own checklist

Now:
- Suggested supplies by room count
- 2-hour arrival windows for eligible local moves
- Standardized blanket wrapping
- Download-style checklist preview card

Make this visually simple, friendly, and easy to scan.

7. TRUST / SOCIAL PROOF SECTION
Include warm stats:
- 12,400+ boxes packed
- 98% local move completion satisfaction
- 4.9/5 average crew friendliness rating
- 1,800+ reusable eco boxes returned

Add testimonial cards from fictional customers. Make it clear they are sample content by using realistic but generic names like “Maya R.”, “Jordan P.”, “Alina S.”

8. MOVING TIMELINE SECTION
Title:
“Your calmer move in 4 steps”
Steps:
1. Tell us what’s moving
2. Pick packing options
3. Meet your crew
4. Settle in with fewer surprises

Each step should have friendly microcopy and match the changelog theme by highlighting which steps were recently improved.

9. PRICING / PACKAGE PREVIEW
Static pricing cards only, no checkout.
Cards:
- Starter Move — for studio apartments
- Family Move — for 2–3 bedroom homes
- Full Nest Move — packing + moving + storage help

Each card should include mock starting price text like “From $249”, feature bullets, and a CTA button “Request Estimate”. Add a small note: “Sample pricing only. Final estimates vary by distance, volume, and date.”

10. FAQ SECTION
Create an FAQ with 5 questions:
- Are these updates available everywhere?
- Do I need to book online?
- Can I use only packing services?
- Are eco boxes included?
- Is this a real booking form?

Answers should clarify this is a static demo style page and content can be sample/mock.

11. FINAL CTA
Headline:
“Ready for a move that feels more organized?”
Text:
“Explore the latest MoveNest improvements and plan your next move with fewer unknowns.”
CTA buttons:
- “View Changelog”
- “Start Estimate”

12. FOOTER
Include:
- MoveNest logo/text
- Short brand line: “Friendly moving updates for calmer moving days.”
- Links: Services, Changelog, Reviews, FAQ
- Small legal-style text: “Static demo content. No real booking or payment is processed.”

INTERACTION DETAILS
- Smooth hover states for cards and buttons
- Upvote-style buttons should be visual only; no real persistence needed
- FAQ accordion can be static or simple front-end state only
- No API calls
- No data fetching
- No maps, no live rates, no real address validation
- No account/login/signup system

RESPONSIVE REQUIREMENTS
- Desktop: hero with two-column layout, cards in grid
- Tablet: cards wrap nicely
- Mobile: single-column layout, readable spacing, nav simplified
- Buttons should be easy to tap
- Text should not overflow

CONTENT TONE
Use friendly moving-company language:
- helpful, calm, organized, careful, reliable
- avoid aggressive sales tone
- make the changelog feel human and customer-focused

IMPORTANT
This is a static website only. Use mock changelog entries, mock comments, mock pricing, and mock stats. Do not integrate real ProductHunt, maps, calendars, payment providers, forms that submit anywhere, databases, or backend services.",

  "provider": "novita",
  "pinned_on": "2026-10-09",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "rubric_id": "rva1:mean(visual,query,asset)"
 }

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
